svg.title: The bicycle's NEAR handlebar grip, and the reason the bar is two parts. The bar the rider's hands were solved to runs along y = 300, and it was drawn on `mount-deck` alone - which is z 2, behind every part of the figure. Measured on the composite, the rider covers an unbroken span from x 56 to x 249 at that row, in every bike pose and in both costumes, so not one pixel of the bar reached the render and a blind `make verify-art` run recorded "hands ON the bar" ABSENT while the bar was in the file the whole time. This is the piece that is NEARER the camera than the rider, at `mount-fore`'s z 29, for the same reason a toboggan's prow is: the near grip is the southernmost point of the bicycle, so it is genuinely in front of a chest that sits further from the camera than it does. It emerges from the FIST, not from the wrist: the hand pivot is solved to y 300, but the mitt ART hangs down and forward of its own pivot, so a grip drawn on the pivot line butted the white cuff and read as an object lying on the coat. Measured instead against the drawn fist - ink edge x 170, mitt body x 176, steady within 2 px over y 314-326 across both costumes and all three bike states - the grip ends at x 167, where its ink merges with the mitt's own outline so the bar reads as passing behind the hand rather than in front of it. The end is a slate disc because in this three-quarter view the near grip points at the camera, so its cut end is seen very nearly face on; it is also the one light note on a dark grip against a dark coat. Static in every frame: `mount-deck` and `mount-fore` carry [0, 0, 0] in every key of `bike/idle`, `bike/walk` and `bike/run`, so the bar cannot pop, slide or change length while the pedals turn. Drawn oversized as section 11.3 requires of all equipment - about 40 px of grip past the fist, where a scale grip would be swallowed whole by a cartoon mitt. The whole window sits inside x 0..240, so it adds nothing to `figureSpan` and moves no stop.
